experiment: P4j matched CUDA Graph deployment for compact heterogeneous route
research_question: When both the shared MLCNN baseline and compact heterogeneous route use the same fixed-shape CUDA Graph deployment protocol, does the compact route convert its near-equal MAC count into acceptable batch-one latency without changing outputs?

frozen_parent.p4h: width-4 compact route has 0.34 percent MAC overhead but eager batch-one latency gate failed
frozen_parent.p4i: two-stream execution preserved outputs but worsened batch-one latency by 5.89 percent versus compact serial

single_mechanism.candidate: fixed-shape CUDA Graph capture and replay
single_mechanism.fairness: CUDA Graph is applied separately to both legacy_mlcnn_global and mlcnn_iq_grouped_task_routed_w4

benchmark_protocol.timing: CUDA events including copy into the static graph input and graph replay
benchmark_protocol.memory: peak CUDA allocated bytes including graph-private pools

deployment_boundary: CUDA Graph evidence applies only to fixed input shapes and stable memory addresses. Dynamic batch or signal length requires separate capture buckets or eager fallback.
stop_rule: Do not alter graph capture mode, warmup, replay protocol or gates after reading results. If matched CUDA Graphs fail either batch-one latency gate, stop launch-overhead-only optimization and move to a genuinely shared or fused front end. Do not train the compact route until a deployment mechanism passes.
next_if_pass: Freeze the graph runner and preregister fresh-identity three-seed compact-route accuracy training, followed by two new-seed confirmation and five-seed statistics.
